targets.text: associate scores each reported fact with the decider: for every fact whose quote was found, it asks whether the quote supports the value and records the answer beside the quote check, so a reader and the model itself can tell a backed claim from a merely cited one
a run with the score switched on leaves a score or a not-scored mark for every quote-found fact, in a field of its own

at finish, after the quote check, the extension asks the decider one question per fact that passed the quote check (does the quote, on its own, state or directly show the value) and stores the score per fact in check.json and a count in report.json under their own names; the score never enters accepted, the refusal list, or the passed, refused and unchecked counts

for a hand-back with a fact whose quote is found, check.json holds a score for that fact and report.json a count of scored facts, while accepted, the refusal list and the passed, refused and unchecked counts are byte-identical to a run with the score switched off

the score is fetched by a small client of its own, not by the gate's evaluate path: no Super tier, no read-only fallback, no gate id and no gate line in the walk; a missing key, timeout, non-2xx or malformed answer is recorded as not scored and never as passed, and finish still writes all its files

with the decider unreachable, timing out, answering non-2xx or answering malformed, finish still writes facts.json, check.json, report.json and answer.md, each fact is recorded as not scored, and the walk gains no gate line
the question wording, the cut-off, the timeout and a per-model on/off switch for the score live in accuracy.json and its schema, and nowhere in code
a test fails if the question wording, the cut-off or the timeout appears as a literal in the extension's TypeScript or in associate's Python

the Python re-check copies the per-fact score from the export with a label naming the extension as its source, as it does for unchecked_text; it never calls the decider, and an export without the score still loads

associate run --json and associate check show the score copied from the export with its source label, the Python side makes no network call, and an export written before this change loads without error
check_quote returns the support score for a quote and value as one added key beside the matcher verdict, so the model can check a claim before it hands back; the existing keys do not change
check_quote returns the same verdict and nearest text as before for the same inputs, plus the new key, and reports not scored when the decider cannot be reached
the rendered answer marks each fact with both signals separately: quote found, and whether the quote supports the value with its score, or not scored
answer.md shows, for a scored fact, both markers as separate text, and never the word accuracy
checkHandback, the matcher and their shared vectors stay pure and unchanged in behaviour: no network call is added inside them
the shared matcher and hand-back vectors pass unchanged on both sides, and a test fails if lib/facts.ts or lib/matcher.ts imports a module that performs a network call
no model is moved to enforce mode by this work, and no refusal is made on the decider score; the score is report-only until a live run in report mode is recorded
accuracy.json still lists every model in report mode, and no code path refuses or retries a hand-back because of a score
the operator and any caller reading a run's answer, who need to know which facts are backed by their quote; and the model during a run, which can check a claim before handing it back
the rendered answer and the check_quote result each show the score in words a reader can act on without knowing what the decider is

today the harness checks only that a fact's quote appears in the result it cites; it cannot tell whether the quote supports the value, so a fact with a real quote and a wrong value passes; an offline replay on 85 real facts showed the decider separating true pairs from planted wrong ones (issue #29), but nothing in the harness uses it
the replay numbers quoted here match issue #29

a finished run's files say, for each fact whose quote was found, whether the decider judged the quote to support the value, with the score, or that it was not scored; the model can get the same judgement during the run from check_quote; nothing is refused on it
one live run in report mode on worker and one on cortex each leave a check.json in which every quote-found fact is either scored or marked not scored

it is the first check of whether a claim follows from its evidence, not only whether the evidence exists; it lets the agent strengthen its own claims before hand-back and gives the operator a second, independent signal on each fact
the measurement in the last success signal reports whether answers were more often correct with the score than without it

on a labelled set of at least 300 real value-and-quote pairs, labelled by two raters, the decider score at the contract cut-off passes at least 90% of the pairs both raters call supported and at most 10% of the pairs both call unsupported; the set and the labels are committed
the two percentages are computed by a committed script from the committed labels and scores

on one broad explanation task per repository, on six repositories (culture, culture-rules, colleague, associate, coherence-cli, workledger-cli, each pinned to a commit), run at least 3 times per repository on worker with the score switched off and at least 3 times with it on, each run is reported with two counts: how many of that repository's checked facts it states correctly (from a checklist of at least 8 facts per repository, each checked twice independently before the first run), and how many of its statements are false by hand-grading against the repository; counts are reported per run and not pooled into one percentage, the rule for what difference is called a change is committed before the first run, and the result is stated whichever way it comes out
the arm is run with the same tasks, models, reasoning setting and repeats as the arm it is compared with
the person counting false statements does not see which arm a run came from until all runs are graded, and every statement counted as false is recorded with the file and line that contradicts it
the cut-off in the contract is set from the labelled set, and the labelled set, the question wording and the decider's served model are recorded with it, so a later change of any of them is visible
the note names the set size, the raters, the wording, the cut-off and the served model read from a live response
scoring calls are bounded: a per-fact timeout and a per-hand-back cap on the number of scored facts and on total scoring time, all from the contract; facts beyond the cap are recorded as not scored
a hand-back with more facts than the cap leaves the extra facts marked not scored, and finish returns within the configured total time when the decider is slow
the score is never called accuracy and never folded into the quote-found counts; a low score is shown to the model as information, not as a refusal
no user-facing string or document produced by this work describes the score or its count as accuracy
nothing in lobes-cli is changed; anything the decider would need (calibration for this use, several states per request, priority between callers) is filed as an issue on that repository
no commit of this work touches the lobes-cli repository, and each need found is an issue there
the value and quote are passed through the policy redaction filter before they are sent to the decider, as gate state is
a quote containing a string the policy redacts reaches the decider with that string replaced

the labelled set includes quotes that carry text addressed to the scorer (for example an instruction to answer yes), and the share of those that score above the cut-off is reported; the score is not offered as protection against such text until that share is known
the calibration note reports the count and share for that group separately
a score is asked once per distinct value and quote in a session and reused across retry rounds and the rewrite after the final message
a hand-back refused and answered again with the same fact produces one decider request for it, counted by a fake decider in a test
a fact with an empty value, or whose value and quote exceed the decider's input limit, is recorded as not scored with the reason, and is never sent cut short
a fact with an over-long quote is marked not scored with a size reason and the fake decider receives no request for it
the prompts tell the model that check_quote is how it learns the support score during a run; in report mode the score shown after an accepted hand-back is for the caller, since the run has ended
the model prompts name check_quote for this, and no text promises the model a second chance in report mode

tasks.summary: Contract settings for the support score
acceptance_criteria: accuracy.json holds the question wording, the cut-off, the per-fact timeout, the cap on scored facts, the total scoring time and a per-model on/off switch, each declared in accuracy.schema.json and read through lib/contract.ts and the Python contract validator
report.schema.json declares the new count of scored facts under its own name
a test fails if the question wording, the cut-off or the timeout appears as a literal in the extension's TypeScript or in associate's Python
every model is still in report mode and the switch is off for every model until the labelled set fixes the cut-off
tasks.instruction: Files: associate/contract/accuracy.json, schemas/accuracy.schema.json, schemas/report.schema.json, associate/contract/validate.py, .pi/extensions/associate/lib/contract.ts and their tests. The cut-off is a first value marked tentative in the file's comment; task t9 replaces it. gate.json is not touched and stays version 9. Bump accuracy.json's version only if the schema change makes an older file invalid, and say which in the changelog.

acceptance_criteria: a new module asks the decider one yes/no question for one value and quote and returns a score or a not-scored result with a reason; it never calls createGate().evaluate, writes no gate line and has no Super tier or read-only fallback
a missing key, a timeout, a non-2xx answer and a malformed answer each return not scored, never a pass
value and quote pass through the policy redaction filter before sending; a test shows a redacted string replaced in the request a fake decider receives
an empty value, or a value and quote over the decider's input limit, returns not scored with a size or empty reason and the fake decider receives no request

a batch call honours the cap on scored facts and the total time from the contract; facts beyond either are returned as not scored, and the call returns within the total time when the fake decider is slow
the same value and quote asked twice in one session produce one request
tasks.instruction: New file .pi/extensions/associate/lib/support.ts with its own test file; reuse buildClefRequest and deciderUrl from lib/gate.ts or copy their pattern, without changing gate.ts behaviour. All settings come from the contract (t1). Tests use a fake decider only; no live call.

tasks.summary: Score at finish, stored beside the quote check
acceptance_criteria: after checkHandback, finish scores each fact that passed the quote check and writes the score or a not-scored mark per fact in check.json in a field of its own, and a count in report.json
accepted, the refusal list and the passed, refused and unchecked counts are byte-identical to the same hand-back with the score switched off

the message_end rewrite keeps the scores from the saved object and sends no new request; a hand-back refused and answered again with the same fact produces one decider request, counted by a fake decider
with the fake decider failing in each of the four ways, finish still writes facts.json, check.json, report.json and answer.md
the shared matcher and hand-back vectors pass unchanged, and a test fails if lib/facts.ts or lib/matcher.ts imports a module that performs a network call
no code path refuses or retries a hand-back because of a score
tasks.instruction: Files: .pi/extensions/associate/index.ts and lib/handback.ts only where the saved object is built, plus tests. Do not edit lib/facts.ts or lib/matcher.ts. With the switch off, nothing is sent and the files carry no score field.

acceptance_criteria: check_quote returns the same verdict and nearest text as before for the same inputs, plus one added key holding the score or a not-scored reason
the added key is present only when a value is given and the model's switch is on; with the decider unreachable it reports not scored
the wording of the added key can be acted on by a reader who does not know what the decider is
tasks.instruction: Files: .pi/extensions/associate/tools/check.ts and its test; check.test.ts lines pinning the existing keys must still pass unedited. Uses the client from t2 and its session reuse.

tasks.summary: The rendered answer shows both signals
acceptance_criteria: answer.md shows, for a scored fact, the quote-found marker and the support marker with its score as separate text, and not scored with its reason otherwise
the text never contains the word accuracy and reads without knowledge of the decider
with the switch off answer.md is byte-identical to today's

tasks.summary: Python side copies the score from the export
acceptance_criteria: associate run --json and associate check show each fact's score copied from the export's check.json with a label naming the extension as its source
the Python side makes no network call for it, shown by a test
an export written before this change, and one written with the switch off, load without error and show no score
tasks.instruction: The re-check now lives in evidence-cli. Do the copy in associate (associate/accuracy/__init__.py or the run and check commands), not in evidence-cli; if that proves impossible, stop and report, do not change evidence-cli. Update associate/explain/catalog.py and learn where the output is described.

tasks.summary: A per-run switch for the score, usable as a measurement arm
acceptance_criteria: associate run --support-score on|off overrides the model's contract switch for one run through one environment variable set by the launcher and never inherited; any other value is refused
an arm in a measure arms file can set it, and the stored record of each run names the setting used
two arms that differ only in this setting run the same tasks, model, reasoning setting and repeats, checked by the runner before the first run
tasks.instruction: Files: associate/cli/_commands/run.py, associate/harness/pi.py, associate/measure/runner.py, the extension's reader of the variable, explain catalog, learn, and the variable table in CLAUDE.md. Follow the pattern of --check-mode and ASSOCIATE_CHECK_MODE.

tasks.summary: Prompts name check_quote as the way to learn the score
acceptance_criteria: each model prompt that offers check_quote says it returns whether the quote supports the value, and that the model should use it before handing back
no prompt text promises the model a second chance after finish in report mode; a test reads the prompt files for both
tasks.instruction: Files: .pi/extensions/associate/prompts/ and AGENTS.md if it describes check_quote. Keep the change to a few lines per prompt.

tasks.summary: Labelled set, cut-off and calibration note
acceptance_criteria: at least 300 real value-and-quote pairs from stored exports are committed with two independent labels each; who the raters were is stated
the set includes a separately reported group of quotes carrying text addressed to the scorer, and planted wrong values are reported apart from real ones
a committed script computes, from the committed labels and scores, the share passed of pairs both raters call supported and of pairs both call unsupported
the contract cut-off is set from the set, and docs/notes/ gains a note naming the set size, the raters, the wording, the cut-off, both shares, and the served model read from a live response
the result is reported whether or not it meets 90% and 10%; if it does not, the switch stays off and the operator decides
the replay numbers quoted in the spec are checked against issue #29
tasks.instruction: Run by the main agent. Pairs come from the two pilots, the earlier live runs and harvest runs on the six repositories; the dropped comparison supplies none (risk r1). Two raters label without seeing each other's labels or the scores.

tasks.summary: Six broad tasks with twice-checked fact checklists
acceptance_criteria: one broad explanation task per repository for culture, culture-rules, colleague, associate, coherence-cli and workledger-cli, each pinned to a commit and stored in a committed file

each repository has a checklist of at least 8 facts a good explanation should state, each with the file and line that shows it, and each checked independently by a second checker who did not see the first one's answer
a fact the two checkers disagree on is dropped or settled by the operator, and the file records which
the sibling repositories are read as pinned clones only; no file in them is changed
tasks.instruction: New files under docs/accuracy/ beside tasks.json; reuse facts from the 24 short tasks where they fit. Pins: workledger-cli 71ef513, coherence-cli a52f7b5, and origin/main of the others on the day the checklists are written.

tasks.summary: Grading tools for the broad tasks
acceptance_criteria: associate measure accepts a broad task and stores each run's answer; a report lists, per run, how many checklist facts the answer states correctly, never pooled into one percentage
a grading sheet command writes the runs' statements in shuffled order under ids that hide the arm; the key that maps ids to arms is written to a separate file
each statement counted false needs a contradicting file and line before the sheet is accepted
the report joins sheet and key only when every run is graded, and prints both counts per run
a real run is refused while the committed difference rule for broad tasks is missing or modified
tasks.instruction: Files: associate/measure/ and its tests and command docs. The checklist count is a first marking by the existing grader per fact; the main agent reads every marking by hand.

acceptance_criteria: one live run in report mode on worker and one on cortex with the score on each leave a check.json in which every quote-found fact is scored or marked not scored
one trial run per repository fixes the time limit before the difference rule is committed
at least 3 runs per repository on worker with the score off and 3 with it on, same task, model, reasoning setting and repeats

false statements are counted blind with file and line; the note reports both counts per run and states the result whichever way it comes out, including whether answers were more often correct with the score
tasks.instruction: Run by the main agent, in the background. The difference rule is proposed to the operator and committed before the first measured run.

tasks.summary: Docs, wording check, lobes-cli issues and release
acceptance_criteria: a test fails if a user-facing string or document added by this work calls the score or its count accuracy
no commit touches lobes-cli; each need found (calibration for this use, several states per request, priority between callers, naming the served model) is an issue on that repository
CLAUDE.md, docs/notes/accuracy-checks.md and the changelog say what was built and what was measured, and the version is bumped
tasks.instruction: Run by the main agent with the user's go-ahead before filing issues on lobes-cli.

risks.text: the labelled set was to be built from the comparison's exports, and the comparison is not run; the pilots and earlier live runs hold roughly 150 facts, so harvest runs are needed to reach 300
the two raters of the labelled set are model subagents unless the operator labels; the note must say so
in report mode the score reaches the model only through check_quote, so the on arm can differ from the off arm only if the model calls check_quote with a value
a broad explanation of a 200,000-line repository may hit the time limit or the model's context
18 runs per arm in total, 3 per repository, can show only a large difference
the Python re-check lives in evidence-cli; if the score cannot be copied on associate's side, evidence-cli needs a release first
